question: Provide a broad company research overview covering the business and revenue mix; financial snapshot and trajectory; balance sheet, debt and working capital; operating cash flow and cash conversion; management narrative versus reported numbers; explicit guidance and capital allocation; and a concise bull and bear case. Include material governance concerns, auditor qualifications, contingent liabilities and related-party risks where supported. State source periods and consolidated versus standalone scope. Identify missing evidence without inventing a four-quarter or multi-year comparison.

report.title: TCS Company Research Brief

findings.statement: TCS generates revenue across multiple industry verticals led by Banking, Financial Services and Insurance at 38.7%, followed by Consumer Business at 15.9%, Communication, Media and Technology at 14.8%, Life Sciences and Healthcare at 10.4%, Manufacturing at 10.0%, and Others at 10.2% for FY 2026.
Geographically, North America represents 48.6% of revenue, United Kingdom 17.4%, and Continental Europe 15.4% in FY 2026.
In FY 2026, TCS achieved revenue of ₹ 267,021 crore, representing a year-over-year growth of 4.6% (a 2.4% decline on a constant currency basis due to a large India transformation program ending).
Operating profit for FY 2026 reached ₹ 66,838 crore with an operating margin of 25.0%, representing a 70 basis point improvement over FY 2025.
Over the past five financial years, TCS recorded a revenue CAGR of 10.2% and an EPS CAGR of 10.3%.
Earnings per share stood at ₹ 145.99 in FY 2026 compared to ₹ 134.19 in FY 2025.

Total funds invested stood at ₹ 50,020 crore as of FY 2026, comprising ₹ 34,887 crore in mutual funds, Government securities and others, ₹ 10,433 crore in bank deposits, ₹ 1,500 crore in inter-corporate deposits, and ₹ 3,200 crore in cash and bank balances.

Standalone related party transactions include inter-corporate deposits for working capital of ₹ 6 crore to TRIL Bengaluru Real Estate Five Limited and ₹ 44 crore to TRIL Bengaluru Real Estate Six Limited as at March 31, 2026, alongside ₹ 1,000 crore to Tata Capital Limited and ₹ 500 crore to Tata Capital Housing Finance Limited.
TCS reported cash conversion ratios of 99.8% in FY 2026 and 96.6% in FY 2025.

Management highlights resilient constant-currency dynamics and strong TCV, while reported numbers reflect a 4.6% nominal revenue increase alongside a 2.4% constant currency decline driven by the conclusion of a large Indian transformation program.
Management expects to benefit from enhanced scale efficiency as growth improves, while continuing to optimize cost structures and maintain disciplined execution.
The bull case is supported by industry-leading return on equity (51.4% in FY 2026), robust cash conversion, and sustained large deal wins in AI and digital transformation.

The bear case features headwinds from legal contingencies, such as a lawsuit from Computer Sciences Corporation resulting in a provision of US$ 112 million, and severance expenses of ₹ 1,388 crore for workforce restructuring.
